name: VA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jennifer McClellan running for re-election
Challenger Robert Murray has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively to McClellan: a D+17 district, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge over a challenger with no reported money. Markets price a Democratic win near certain, and no polling or ratings evidence suggests movement toward Republicans.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or polling showing a much tighter race would be the first sign of trouble, but nothing currently indicates one.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 4th District is a solidly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward Democrats. First-term incumbent Jennifer McClellan is running for re-election after easily securing her party's nomination, and she has raised over $1.1 million for the race. Republican challenger Robert Murray has no reported fundraising on file, and an independent candidate also appears on the ballot.

With no public general-election polling and no expert raters flagging the race, the outlook rests on fundamentals, which all favor the incumbent. Prediction markets put McClellan's chances at roughly 96 percent. The district's composition and the money gap make an upset highly unlikely; the main open question is the size of the winning margin, not the winner.
